messages:
sana: FYI intake for a community model (PoppyNet-12B). License language is kind of fuzzy about "non-commercial" vs "research". Want to onboard for a Private pilot in EMEA — anyone looked at this one yet?

izzy: Share link and license snippet so we can triage hosting/packaging risk. Repo mentioned a "no-redistribute" clause last week in another PR.

sana: https://example.com/poppynet/repo (copied from README). License excerpt copied below:

```
Redistribution of model weights is prohibited.
Weights may be used for internal evaluation and research.
Commercial use requires a separate license.
```

arthur: @sana thanks. Short answers up front: 1) Running behind our hosted API likely counts as commercial hosting; 2) Bundling or shipping weights to customers = redistribution (likely prohibited); 3) Quantization may be a "derivative" — depends on how they word it. Need to verify upstream license + any CLA/third-party obligations.

jake: Product context: customer is a mid-market SaaS, wants to run PoppyNet in their private VPC for a paid feature. They will not re-distribute weights externally, but they will pay for the SaaS feature. Does that qualify as "commercial" per the license?

arthur: Yes, running a paid feature usually falls under commercial use. If they obtain weights directly from upstream under a commercial license, we can help run it. If we provide the weights or a packaged appliance, that's redistribution. If customer brings their own weights and we only provide runtime, that's lower risk but still needs an explicit check.

izzy: For Private deployments we sometimes package models into an AMI/container. That would look like redistribution. Could we instead add a BYOW (bring-your-own-weights) flow that streams the weights into the customer's VPC without us holding them?

arthur: That's a good engineering workaround. Legal reqs: confirm provenance, confirm upstream doesn't forbid derivatives, and confirm export-control language. If they forbid derivatives, quantization could be risky. Actionable: I will reach out to upstream and draft a permissions template.

legal-bot: created ticket ML-LEGAL-372: "PoppyNet licensing review". Labels: license-review, export-control, byow-consideration.

sana: Timeline: customer wants a 2-week pilot. We need a quick gating decision: safe to proceed with BYOW in private VPC pending upstream reply?

arthur: Proposed gating checklist for eng-ml (quick):
- confirm exact license file and version from upstream (sha)
- confirm whether weights were trained with any third-party data with special restrictions
- confirm whether license explicitly disallows derivatives (quantization)
- confirm upstream contact + permission for commercial hosting OR get written permission
- grep repo for export-control / EAR / ITAR keywords and flag if present
- mark model in catalog as "restricted-hosting" / "no-redistribution" until cleared

sana: Copying that into intake form now. Also note: repo README mentions "proprietary TPU image" and a short hardware note — could be export-control relevant.

izzy: Tech follow-ups I put on the ticket: implement BYOW bootstrap for Private, add enforcement to console to block packaging the weights, and add a vendor verification field.

jake: I'll let the customer know we can run a BYOW pilot but need them to fetch weights directly and provide a proof of acquisition.

arthur: I'll ping upstream legal and request a commercial hosting license + clarify derivative/quantization. If they refuse, recommendation: do not package or redistribute, consider only supporting BYOW and add a clear "usage restrictions" warning in the model catalog.

sana: Great. Leaving this thread open — will update when upstream replies. cc @arthur @izzy @jake :thumbsup:

(End of thread)
